endorsements.quote: There is also a need for digital health literacy curricula that explicitly teach adolescents how to interrogate algorithmic claims.

This ecosystem must include algorithmic transparency summaries that are accessible to young readers, uniform labeling of AI-generated health content, and safety protocols that monitor for misinterpretation patterns over time.

Without protective design patterns such as calibrated uncertainty displays, graded information depth, and age-responsive prompting, these interactions risk replacement of human guidance with algorithmic guidance without developmental alignment.

unlisted_practices: Clinicians should ask adolescents about their use of symptom checkers, chatbots, wearable interpretations, and health apps as a routine part of pediatric assessment.
Designers and regulators should treat the pediatric environment as a distinct ecosystem requiring developmental protocols.
Developers should provide visible signals to users about when and why AI outputs have changed after model updates or drift.
Developers should design AI tools with age-responsive prompting and graded information depth for young users.
Regulators should align regulatory structures with children's developmental needs.

screen.reason: This is an editorial providing recommendations and developmental design frameworks for safer pediatric human-AI interaction in digital health.
